title: Host-course GenAI customization mini-project
summary: Graduate AI students complete a two-week module on prompting, fine-tuning, and retrieval-augmented generation, then propose and build a GenAI tool related to the host course. Students validate model responses against reliable sources, customize the model where needed, and obtain peer reviews from classmates.

sources.title: A PBL-Based Mini Course Module for Teaching Computer Science Students to Utilize Generative AI for Enhanced Learning

locator.section: III. Course Structure and Implementation, 3. Mini-Project

sources.evidence_quote: After the lectures and hands-on labs, we require students to initiate a mini-project that they propose themselves.

assessment.summary: Design a GenAI application that applies host-course knowledge or helps other students learn it, validate its answers, and improve it using fine-tuning or RAG.
student_actions: Develop a GenAI tool or learning application.
Validate ChatGPT responses against books, videos, or articles.
Collect and preprocess grounding or fine-tuning data.
Apply fine-tuning or RAG when responses are deficient.
Have classmates use and peer-review the model.

student_role.description: Students build, validate, and customize a GenAI system relevant to host-course content.

grading.method: Projects are evaluated using peer reviews from classmates who use the customized model.

reported_results: Mean self-rating for prompt-engineering skill increased from 3.3 before the module to 4.9 afterward.
